source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with Alzheimer's becomes more agitated and wanders in the late afternoon. This is:
questions.rationale: Sundowning: agitation and disorientation in afternoon and evening, middle stage.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Alzheimer's Stages (PDF p. 437)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Donepezil is given in Alzheimer's disease to:
questions.rationale: Cholinesterase inhibitors increase brain acetylcholine; memantine blocks NMDA.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Alzheimer's Management (PDF p. 437)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which intervention promotes safety for a client with Alzheimer's at home?
questions.rationale: Secure doors, remove hazards, supervise, avoid restraints.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Alzheimer's Safety (PDF p. 438)
questions.quote: Secure the doors from the house

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: At mealtime, a client with Alzheimer's is best helped by:
options: Offering one dish at a time
questions.rationale: Keep meals simple: one dish at a time, small pieces, familiar foods.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Alzheimer's Nutrition (PDF p. 438)
questions.quote: One dish is offered at a time

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Sudden unilateral facial paralysis with inability to close one eye suggests:
questions.rationale: Bell's palsy is CN VII inflammation causing unilateral facial weakness.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bell's Palsy (PDF p. 438)
questions.quote: Unilateral inflammation of the seventh cranial nerve

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Why are artificial tears used in Bell's palsy?
questions.rationale: Incomplete eyelid closure exposes the cornea.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bell's Palsy Nursing (PDF p. 439)
questions.quote: Artificial tears is recommended (prevents corneal irritation)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with Bell's palsy should be taught to:
questions.rationale: Soft diet, chew on unaffected side, avoid hot food, do facial exercises.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bell's Palsy Nursing (PDF p. 439)
questions.quote: Instruct to chew on the unaffected side

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Involuntary jerky movements, cognitive decline, and family history at age 40 suggest:
questions.rationale: Huntington's is inherited, with chorea and progressive dementia; genetic counseling advised.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Huntington's Disease (PDF p. 440)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Brief, stabbing facial pain triggered by brushing the teeth suggests:
questions.rationale: Tic douloureux: paroxysmal pain along CN V, triggered by touch.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Trigeminal Neuralgia (PDF p. 440)
questions.quote: Intense recurring episodes of pain (sudden, jabbing, burning or knifelike)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which drug is commonly used for trigeminal neuralgia?
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Trigeminal Neuralgia (PDF p. 441)

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which measure helps prevent attacks of trigeminal neuralgia?
questions.rationale: Avoid extreme temperatures, jarring, and vigorous facial care.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Trigeminal Nursing (PDF p. 441)
questions.quote: Food that is too hot or too cold

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which bone cells dissolve and resorb bone?
questions.rationale: Osteoclasts resorb; osteoblasts form; osteocytes maintain.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bone Cells (PDF p. 442)
questions.quote: Osteoclasts- are multi nuclear cells involved in dissolving and resorbing bone

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The shaft of a long bone is the:
questions.rationale: Diaphysis is the shaft; epiphyses are the ends.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Parts of the Bone (PDF p. 442)
questions.quote: Diaphysis- shaft of the long bone

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the first stage of fracture healing?
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bone Healing (PDF p. 442)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Complete bone remodeling after a fracture can take:
questions.rationale: Calcification within about 6 weeks; full remodeling 6 months to 1 year.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bone Healing (PDF p. 442)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The knee and elbow are examples of which joint type?
questions.rationale: Hinge joints bend in one direction; hip and shoulder are ball-and-socket.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Articular System (PDF p. 443)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Pushing against an immovable wall is which muscle contraction?
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Muscle Contraction (PDF p. 443)
questions.quote: Isometric contraction, the length of the muscles remains constant

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A fluid-filled sac that cushions tendons at friction points is a:
questions.rationale: Bursae reduce friction; ligaments bind bones.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Articular System (PDF p. 443)
questions.quote: Bursa- sac filled with synovial fluid
